brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0 and piece:0,-1,0 are full bases, piece:-1,0,0 is a south-half base. They are bolted together (jointBolt x2) and the open edges are capped.

bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 and bin:0,-1,0~hex-bin-full-div2 drop into their cells and hang on their own rims, so you can lift them out without any fixings. They hold M3 screws, nuts, standoffs and a solder reel.
drawer:0#-1,0#cut sits on the half base and holds a pile of screws. Shown open, it would hit an end cap by 0.54 mm (the limit is 0.50 mm), so the build shows it closed.
handle:0,0,0;top is mounted on the top cover over the main bin. The configurator checks fit only, not whether the handle and joints can take the load of carrying the filled organizer.

finish.summary: Small three-cell organizer, 29 printed parts, about 1741 g of filament. It has two full hex bases and one south-half base. The bases are joined with joint bolts and every open edge is closed with solid caps. There are two drop-in bins: bin:0,0,0 with three compartments under a lid, and bin:0,-1,0 with two compartments and no lid. A drawer sits on the cut face of the half base. A carry handle is fixed to the lid (cover:0,0,0;full;top) on top of the three-compartment bin. The bins hold screws, nuts, standoffs and a solder reel, and the drawer holds screws. The final check shows no rule errors, and the mesh-collision check came back clear. Some limits: the drawer shown open would hit an end cap by 0.54 mm, so I left it closed. The props in the lidded bin and the drawer can't be seen in the render. The handle only carries the lidded cell, and the configurator doesn't check carry strength.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
